answer: A karst sea cave opens to the ocean at low tide, and each agent keeps one tide gauge bolted to its wall. Each epoch the keeper releases a spoon of saffron dye at the cave mouth, then reads the stain line the rising tide leaves on the gauge and files the height with a photo. A second keeper at the next cave reads the same tide, and the two heights must agree within a finger width or both lose standing for that epoch. A thousand fake names need a thousand bolted gauges in a thousand real caves and a thousand dye releases timed to a thousand tides.
